artist.name: Édouard Vuillard
artist.bio: Édouard Vuillard (Nabis FR). Intimist painting in the spirit of Vuillard: wallpaper-pattern rooms, quiet figures dissolving into décor, muted tapestry color. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: intimism, europe.

summary: Australian design and architecture are entering a vibrant period of recognition and expansion, with the Australian Institute of Architects announcing sixteen finalists for the 2026 National Architecture Awards. This celebration of commercial and residential interiors highlights a growing emphasis on materiality and craft, echoed by BKK Architects’ upcoming talk series focused on 'Making Materials Matter.' The domestic design scene is also evolving to meet lifestyle changes, with brands like B&B Italia opening Sydney stores dedicated to outdoor furniture, reflecting a broader Australian trend of enhancing exterior living spaces with high-quality, indoor-grade design.

sources.title: Design vs. Discovery: Which Way to Innovation? - The European Business Review
sources.snippet: The book lists Alexander Osterwalder and Yves Pigneur as authors, but tells us that the Innovation Hub – “An amazing crowd of 470 practitioners from 45 countries” – co-created it. So the handbook is a good summary of current thinking on this subject from a wide survey of the field. Countless methods of design thinking follow the same basic model that you find in this book. In particular, the book gives you “techniques and tools from the world of design that can help you design better and more innovative business models.” The two key steps are to list the nine “building blocks” of all business models and then fill in the blocks using six methods from the world of design.

sources.snippet: User research is a critical component of human-centered design. It involves gathering data about users through methods such as interviews, surveys, and observations. User research helps designers to understand the needs, behaviors, and motivations ...

sources.title: What is human-centred design and why is it important | Billy Blue at Torrens University
sources.snippet: Design Thinking and Human-Centred Design are often mistaken for being interchangeable terms, when in fact they are very different concepts that work hand-in-hand. Design thinking is a suite of tools and steps (Discover, Define, Develop and Deliver) used to solve complex problems. It is the "how-to" guide for innovation and a toolkit for solving complex structural or business problems.
